evidence.statement: The editor loads title, description, body and tagList, then submits the full form. Body editing preserves title, description and tagList from the accepted producer output.
Article creation returns article.slug; update resolves the same resource through the returned slug path parameter. Native editor fetches and submits using route.params.slug.

business_state_comparison.slug: runtime identity binding; not a cross-route business-equality field

execution_conditions: Restore the same synthetic actor fixture independently before each complete case; authenticate UI and API as that same actor.
Record producer rejection separately and do not execute or credit a consumer dependency when creation did not succeed.
For an accepted producer, retain the actual response and verify the resource exists before continuing; bind the returned slug without guessing it from the title.

Use the accepted producer output to bind title, description and tagList; preserve normalized omitted-tag output. For a native UI edit, verify loaded fields against those bindings, then change only body.
After editing, verify persisted title, description and tagList equal the bound values and body equals the requested new body; treat tagList as an unordered set.
Verify the authenticated owner and resource count against the reset fixture. Perform a fresh native UI GET and confirm the updated body is readable.
Only explicitly observed producer-to-consumer field/state consumption may be submitted as selector coverage; declared targets and attempted calls do not establish exercised edges.
oracle.input_semantics: Operation inputs are templates. A future adapter must resolve the output bindings below before executing the consumer; it must not submit baseline template values over producer-mutated or normalized fields.
